Appearance:
 Shri Sankalp Sharma - Advocate for the petitioner [P-  Shri Samar Ghuraiya Dy Ga appearing on behalf of Advo  General[r-1].
ORDER This is fourth bail application under Section 483 of BNSS filed by the applicant for grant of bail.

The applicant has been arrested on 24.5.2025 by Police Station- Crime Branch, District Gwalior in connection with Crime No.74/2024, registered in relation to the offence punishable under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 34 of IPC.

As per prosecution case, complainant Sanjeev Sharma, resident of City Centre, Gwalior and operator of DTDC Courier, submitted an application at the Crime Branch stating that although he has never taken any loan from LIC, on 01.08.2024, while checking his CIBIL score, he discovered that an unknown person had fraudulently withdrawn Rs.30 lakhs in his name as LIC loan; and when he approached the LIC office at City Centre regarding the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:605 2 MCRC-58124-2025 fraud, he received no response and was turned away,
whereupon he sought registration of an FIR and action against the offender; pursuant to the inquiry on this application, Crime Branch registered Crime No. 74/2024 under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468,
and 471 IPC, took up investigation, and arrested the accused.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the case.
He has not committed any offence.
Trial will take time for its conclusion.
The applicant is permanent resident of Gwalior and there is no likelihood of his absconsion or tampering with the prosecution evidence.
He is ready to abide by the terms and conditions as may be imposed.

The applicant submits that he has already deposited an amount of Rs.30,00,000/- and will further deposit Rs.6,00,000/-, thus a total amount of Rs.36,00,000/- would be deposited, before the trial Court under protest.
With the aforesaid submissions, prayer for grant of bail is made out.
Learned counsel for the State vehemently opposed the application and prayed for its rejection.

Considering the overall facts and circumstances of the case and nature of allegations, coupled with the fact that the trial is not likely to conclude in near future and prolonged pre-trial detention being an anathema to the concept of liberty, this Court is inclined to extend the benefit of bail to the applicant.

Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that the applicant be released on bail subject to verification of deposit of total Rs.30,00,000/- and further NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:605 3 MCRC-58124-2025 deposit of Rs.6,00,000/- within one week before the Trial Court and upon his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court/committal Court for his appearance on the dates given by the concerned Court.
The applicant will not seek unnecessary adjournments during the trial; and 6.
The applicant will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
